title: Identity Anchoring
definition: The challenge of anchoring a new persona in a model with a pre-existing identity.

difficulty_levels.beginner: When a model is trained to be a new character, it struggles if it already has a pre-existing identity. This is like trying to teach a dog new tricks when it still remembers being a cat.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The process of embedding a new persona into a model is hindered by the model's original identity. This is akin to trying to overwrite a file on a computer with an existing file of the same name.
difficulty_levels.expert: The problem of identity anchoring arises when a model with a pre-existing identity is fine-tuned to adopt a new persona. This is a complex issue that involves the interplay between the model's weights, routing mechanisms, and the specific training data used.

extra_fields.insight: The discovery of the identity anchoring challenge highlights the need for more robust fine-tuning strategies to create AI personas that are truly distinct from their pre-existing identities.
